title: Fibrant-target mapping-space detection in an all-cofibrant simplicial model
statement:
Use model categories, weak equivalences, cofibrant and fibrant objects and functorial factorizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], simplicial tensors and cotensors of [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Kan fibrations and trivial Kan fibrations (maps with the right lifting property against all horn, respectively boundary, inclusions) of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicially enriched model category, with these tensors and cotensors, such that for every cofibration $i:A\to B$ and fibration $p:E\to D$ the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B,E)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,E)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,D)}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B,D)$$
is a Kan fibration, trivial if either $i$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. Suppose every object of $\mathcal M$ is cofibrant. For any morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f$ is a weak equivalence if and only if, for every fibrant object $Z$, precomposition induces a weak homotopy equivalence
$$f^*:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y,Z)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Z).$$
All mapping simplicial sets and constructions are taken in fixed containing universes; no properness or combinatorial hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section A.3.1, simplicial model mapping-space calculus (agent extraction of the fibrant-replacement and pi_0-inverse argument in the returned item, Step 4); see also Lemmas 2.2.3.4 and 2.2.3.6 for its slice application. Archival source WANTED; online fetch timed out. No Stacks tag states this general model-category assertion.

proof.text: Write $K\otimes T$ for the chosen tensor. Its enriched adjunction [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] identifies lifting squares from $K\otimes T\to L\otimes T$ against $p:E\to D$ with lifting squares from $K\to L$ against $\operatorname{Map}(T,E)\to\operatorname{Map}(T,D)$. Indeed the two horizontal maps transpose to $K\to\operatorname{Map}(T,E)$ and $L\to\operatorname{Map}(T,D)$; their equality and the two filler equations transpose as well. The simplicial model axiom with $0\to T$ makes this mapping map a Kan fibration, trivial if $p$ is trivial. Here $\operatorname{Map}(0,E)$ is terminal: its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\otimes0\to E$, and $\Delta^n\otimes0$ is initial by the cotensor adjunction. Consequently, for a monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$, its tensor with $T$ lifts against every trivial fibration and is a cofibration. For an endpoint $\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ it lifts against every fibration, since this is a one-dimensional horn. Thus either endpoint tensor is a trivial cofibration. These conclusions use precisely the two lifting-class characterizations in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] and the boundary/horn criteria in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: tensor lifting squares (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: For each $T$, put $C_T=\Delta^1\otimes T$, with endpoints $e_0,e_1:T\to C_T$ and collapse $c_T:C_T\to T$. Tensor preserves the coproduct $\partial\Delta^1=\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0$, as follows immediately by applying its adjunction to maps out of that coproduct. Step 1 makes $(e_0,e_1):T\amalg T\to C_T$ a cofibration and $e_0$ a weak equivalence. Since $c_Te_0=1_T$, two-out-of-three gives $c_T\in W$. Thus $C_T$ is a good cylinder, although its collapse need not be a fibration. For fibrant $Z$, the same simplicial model axiom on $0\to T$ and $Z\to1$ makes $\operatorname{Map}(T,Z)$ Kan. No fibrancy of $T$ has been used.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: the explicit simplicial cylinder (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: Suppose $f\in W$. Factor it, using [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], as $X\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $i$ a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $p$ trivial. The simplicial model axiom on $i$ and $Z\to1$ gives a trivial Kan fibration $i^*:\operatorname{Map}(E,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(X,Z)$; the mapping sets into $1$ are terminal by the tensor adjunction. Because $Y$ is cofibrant, lift its initial map against $p$ to obtain $s:Y\to E$ with $ps=1_Y$. On the boundary of $C_E$, prescribe $sp$ at endpoint 0 and $1_E$ at endpoint 1. Both composites with $p$ equal $p$. The square with left map $E\amalg E\to C_E$, right map the trivial fibration $p$, top map $(sp,1_E)$ and bottom map $pc_E$ therefore has a lift $H:C_E\to E$. Its endpoints are $sp,1_E$, and $pH=pc_E$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: factorization and explicit lifting homotopy (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: Transpose $H$ by [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] to a simplicial path $\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Map}(E,E)$. Enriched composition with this path gives a simplicial homotopy $\operatorname{Map}(E,Z)\times\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Map}(E,Z)$ from $(sp)^*=p^*s^*$ to the identity; at $(a,t)$ its value is $a\circ H_t$. The other composite is $s^*p^*=(ps)^*=1$, with its constant homotopy. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to conclude that $p^*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The trivial Kan fibration $i^*$ is weak by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; two-out-of-three (in particular closure under composition) there gives $f^*=i^*p^*$ weak. This proves the forward implication for every fibrant $Z$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: the two simplicial inverse identities (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: We record explicitly how components are computed, using the quotient realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For any simplicial set $K$, let $S$ be its vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by endpoint pairs of edges, and give $S$ the discrete topology. All vertices of each simplex have the same class, so the maps constant at that class on each geometric simplex descend to a continuous map $|K|\to S$ by the defining quotient topology. Every point of a geometric simplex is joined by a straight path to a vertex. Vertices in a common class are joined by the finite edge zigzag defining that class. Thus each fiber is path connected, and a path cannot change its image in discrete $S$. Hence $S=\pi_0|K|$, naturally in simplicial maps; this includes empty $K$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: components of quotient realization (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: Choose very good cylinders $T\amalg T\to I_T\twoheadrightarrow T$ for $T=X,Y$ using [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], and the sets $h_I(T,Z)$ of [lem-coef-fixed-cylinder-fibrant-target-detection]. Compare them with $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(T,Z)$. In a larger universe form an ordinary localization $\gamma:\mathcal M\to\mathcal H$ by finite strings of arrows and formal inverses of $W$, modulo composition, identity and inverse relations. This construction has the required localization universal property, including natural transformations by applying their naturality to those strings. For fibrant $Z$ choose a good path object by factoring its diagonal into a trivial cofibration and fibration. The criterion of [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] applies both to the good cylinder $C_T$ of Step 2 and to $I_T$: maps $a,b:T\to Z$ have equal localization images exactly when a homotopy with either prescribed cylinder exists. By the tensor adjunction [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], a $C_T$-homotopy is exactly an edge of $\operatorname{Map}(T,Z)$ with vertices $a,b$. The two cylinder relations therefore coincide; they are equivalence relations since both equal equality after $\gamma$. Taking their generated relations, Step 5 gives a bijection $h_I(T,Z)\cong\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(T,Z)$ sending $[a]$ to its component. Since this bijection keeps the representative $a$, the functions induced by precomposition with $f$ correspond exactly.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: comparison with fixed-cylinder homotopy classes (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).

proof.text: Conversely suppose every $f^*$ in the statement is a weak homotopy equivalence. By the definition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] it induces a bijection on path components for each fibrant $Z$. Step 6 identifies that function with $h_I(Y,Z)\to h_I(X,Z)$. Both $X$ and $Y$ are cofibrant by hypothesis, and the cylinders just chosen have cofibration boundary and trivial-fibration collapse, exactly as required by [lem-coef-fixed-cylinder-fibrant-target-detection]. Its converse therefore yields $f\in W$. The constructions take place in the containing universes allowed in the statement. Empty mapping sets cause no exception: the component sets and quotient sets are both empty, and all bijections and lifting arguments above retain their stated meanings.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational simplicial mapping calculus: fibrant-target detection and empty cases (agent-written expansion; HTT A.3.1 not archived).
